title: Trillion Dollar Body
opening: Two people can weigh the same and have different strength, mobility and fitness. Your goal needs to include what you want your body to be able to do. If weight changes but you lose strength you wanted to keep, the plan has not met the whole goal. Compare what you expected with what happens.

modes.label: Weight and capability
modes.description: The same scale reading does not tell you whether someone can perform a strength task, move comfortably or sustain their day. Choose the capability that belongs in the goal.

modes.label: Controls and outcomes
modes.description: Food intake, energy expenditure, protein, muscle stimulus and time interact. Choose gain, maintenance or loss, then name a capability to preserve.

modes.label: Forecast and observation
modes.description: A watch or calculator supplies an estimate, not an observation of exact tissue change. Compare the forecast with appropriate observations over time, including capability and recovery.

statements.text: Body weight is one output, not the whole meaning of physical mastery.
statements.feedback: The framework asks you to consider the physical capability and other outcomes relevant to the person, as well as body composition.

statements.text: Choose gain, maintenance or loss, and name the capability that should be preserved.
statements.feedback: If you reach your weight target but lose the capability you wanted to keep, the plan hasn't met the whole goal.

statements.text: A watch’s expenditure value is an estimate that should be compared with suitable observations.
statements.feedback: It remains an estimate, not a direct observation of every bodily process or change in body tissue.

statements.text: One aggressive personal protocol is the right plan for everyone with the same goal.
statements.feedback: The source warns against universalizing a personal protocol. Suitability, health, recovery and the actual outcome matter.

examples.summary: Someone wants to change their body composition while keeping their strength. They track their weight and repeat the same strength task. If that task gets harder across repeated attempts and they have more trouble recovering, they need to review the plan. The change in weight alone does not tell them whether they kept their strength.
